theory.title: Exercise 2.4.3: Inline List Iteration
theory.content:
⚡ Quick Iteration

MENTOR-9: "Creating a list variable works, but sometimes it's overkill. For small fixed sets, just list the values inline!"

"Clean, direct, and perfectly valid Robot Framework."

📘 Inline List Syntax

Two Approaches:

# Approach 1: List variable (previous exercise)
@{statuses}=    Create List    OPTIMAL    WARNING    CRITICAL
FOR    ${status}    IN    @{statuses}
    Log    ${status}
END

# Approach 2: Inline values (this exercise)
FOR    ${status}    IN    OPTIMAL    WARNING    CRITICAL
    Log    ${status}
END

# Both do the same thing!

💡 When to Use Inline

# ✅ Good for inline: Small, fixed, literal values
FOR    ${color}    IN    red    green    blue
    Log    Color: ${color}
END

FOR    ${level}    IN    DEBUG    INFO    WARN    ERROR
    Log    Level: ${level}
END

# ❌ Better with variable: Dynamic or reused lists
@{systems}=    Get All Systems    # Dynamic list from keyword
FOR    ${sys}    IN    @{systems}
    Check System    ${sys}
END

⚙️ Key Rules

  • 🔹 Values after IN: Each value = one iteration
  • 🔹 Space-separated: Use 4 spaces between values
  • 🔹 No special symbols: Don't use @{} for inline values
  • 🔹 Best for literals: Fixed strings, not dynamic data

🎯 Your Task

Create a FOR loop that iterates through OPTIMAL, WARNING, and CRITICAL status values inline (no list variable).
